methods.label: Choose a convenient common distance
methods.explanation:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Multiplying all segment lengths by the same positive factor multiplies their travel times by that factor too, leaving the average speed unchanged. We can therefore use \(60\) kilometers for each segment to make the times whole numbers.

Time equals distance divided by speed, so the swimming, biking, and running times are respectively
\[
\frac{60}{3}=20,\qquad
\frac{60}{20}=3,\qquad
\frac{60}{10}=6
\]
hours. The total distance is \(180\) kilometers, and the total time is \(20+3+6=29\) hours. Thus the average speed is
\[
\frac{180}{29}=6+\frac{6}{29}\text{ km/h}.
\]
Since \(0<\frac{6}{29}<\frac12\), the average speed lies between \(6\) and \(6.5\). The closest listed speed is \(6\) kilometers per hour, choice \(D\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary distance-speed-time relationships, common scaling, whole-number arithmetic, and fraction comparison, all within AMC 10 scope.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is calculating average speed from total distance and total elapsed time. No supplied node directly captures that target, so assessedIds is empty and a missing node is proposed. cnm_p111 supplies supporting distance-speed-time knowledge; its forward-calculation criteria do not assess average speed across different-speed segments. The method uses cnm_p107 to justify convenient common scaling, cnm_p110 to recover times by division, and cnm_p169 to identify the closest choice. Adding unlike-denominator fractions and dividing by a fraction are unnecessary in this route.

needsNewNodes.name: Average speed over a journey
needsNewNodes.description: Define average speed as total distance traveled divided by total elapsed time. For a journey with several constant-speed segments, determine each segment's time, add the times and distances, and calculate the overall speed using consistent units and positive total time.
needsNewNodes.reason: The question directly assesses combining different-speed segments into one average speed. cnm_p111 covers the basic distance-speed-time relationship, while the catalog's arithmetic-mean nodes do not directly cover this distance-and-time aggregation.

review.mathematicalCheck: For equal segment length d>0, total time is 29d/60 hours, giving average speed 180/29=6+6/29 km/h. Since 0<6/29<1/2, choice D is uniquely closest. The scaling argument and all calculations are valid.
